name: Product-truth in the leafcutter architecture
summary: How product-truth sits inside Leafcutter's architecture: the product-truth store lives beside the acceptance-criteria store, the Atlas reads that store live and renders its flows, and the agents produce and extend the artifacts (flows, mock data, ACs) that both surfaces depend on. Together these three pieces make product-truth a living layer rather than a static document.

steps.label: The Atlas reads it live and renders flows
steps.human:
The Leafcutter Atlas reads the product-truth store and renders its flows. Its current getFlows cache persists for the repository root during the server process; edits do not imply automatic polling or immediate freshness, and this preview is restarted after final generation.

I/O boundary: getFlows() reads flow JSON and adapts it into the existing UI view model. The visible browser tree is rendered React/HTML; it is not the flow JSON sent back as a new result. This process caches parsed flows per repository root, so a running preview may need refresh/restart after source changes.

  flow/steps/*/human: string (required)

steps.label: Agents produce & extend the artifacts
steps.human:
Leafcutter's agents produce and extend the product-truth artifacts — drafting flows, seeding mock data, and generating ACs — keeping the layer alive.

I/O boundary: Agents author flow JSON and parsed AC YAML. This diagram shows artifact ownership, not automatic implementation or approval.

  flow/steps: array (required)
